Wasserstein distance map: candidate dice.py:361-364 computes W(b,v)=sum_k M[y(b,v),k]*p_k. The reference (reference/monai/losses/dice.py:402-414) computes the same quantity through a gather.
Class weights: candidate dice.py:377-378 computes alpha=1/(V+1) with absent classes at 1. The reference (reference/monai/losses/dice.py:456-461) computes the same.

Generalized TP and denominator: candidate dice.py:397-398 and 418-419 use alpha_vox.unsqueeze(1) * (1 - or 2 - W).unsqueeze(0), giving a (B,B,N) product summed to (B,). The reference (reference/monai/losses/dice.py:436, 453) uses (B,1,N)*(B,N), which broadcasts to the same (B,B,N). The batch coupling is therefore identical to the reference and is not a candidate defect.

Loss: candidate dice.py:441-442 returns mean(1 - (2TP+s)/(D+s)), the same as the reference (reference/monai/losses/dice.py:386-388). The reduction setting is stored but not applied in forward on both sides.
Only the minor float64-to-float32 output dtype difference noted under api_contract separates the candidate from the reference numerically.
